title: Power bases in the Dark Medieval
summary: Why every kind of supernatural band builds a shared domain.

claims.text: Mages of every stripe find they are weak alone and strong in company: pagan Fellowships band together to survive, Hermetics and Ahl-i-Batin share ideas, and the Messianic Voices ride on the Church.
Garou packs share a totem and can sway a stretch of land, openly or through Kinfolk, as defenders of the Earth.
The shadow Inquisition keeps strongholds in the towns of Christendom where the Adversary feeds, gaining some worldly power along the way.

title: Pooled Backgrounds
summary: Combining characters’ Backgrounds into a shared demesne.

claims.text: Players can merge their characters’ Backgrounds into a shared power base; a troupe of five could in theory pool around a hundred dots, so the Storyteller needs guidance to keep it in check.
Backgrounds generally cannot be bought with experience, though they can grow with Maturation points.
When a group builds a shared Anchor in play, the Storyteller may optionally ask each player to put in one experience point, except a player whose existing Background it grows from.

title: Rite of Deconsecration
summary: A level four inquisitor ritus that unmakes Holy Ground.

claims.text: Seldom taught to young inquisitors, the rite permanently severs the divine link that gives Holy Ground its miraculous nature.
It takes an hour of undisturbed prayer on the site, usually on one’s knees before a picture of Christ risen, begging pardon, and costs 3 Conviction.
It is meant to keep a sacred site from being turned to evil use, leaving it spiritually inert.

title: Compel the Ghostly Guardian
summary: A level three Mortis ritual for warding a building with a ghost.

claims.text: The Giovanni devised it to guard warehouses and trading posts; few other Cappadocians know it and it is almost unknown outside Italy.
It binds the spirit of someone who died in the building, no larger than a large townhouse, to frighten intruders and warn its master.

The caster needs the dead person’s name and a piece of the body or a cherished belonging, works for five hours and marks every opening in personal blood; some Cappadocians murder someone on site to be sure.

title: Lands of the Fiends
summary: How Tzimisce domains taint the soil.

claims.text: No Cainites are as bound to native land as the Tzimisce, and something unclean clings to ground claimed even by a young Fiend.
Most often the soil turns grey and lifeless, beasts grow sly and vicious even toward people, and mortals become sullen and listless.

title: The brochs of Scotland
summary: Mysterious stone towers in the Highlands.

claims.text: Brochs are small, open-topped stone towers about two storeys high, plain outside but with stones fused by great heat inside, making walls stronger than most castles.
Locals credit the faeries, but the Fianna, who have spoken with the fae, suspect a lost technique of the White Howlers and their Kinfolk.
Peasants shun them, but brigands, Old Faith mages and Gangrel have all made homes in them.

title: Al-Jazari’s locks
summary: Combination strongboxes of the Muslim world.

claims.text: A late 12th-century treatise on clever mechanisms describes a strongbox with eight dials and some four billion combinations, and Middle Eastern nobles and merchants now have chests and doors built on its principles.
The Ahl-i-Batin wonder whether al-Jazari was one of their own, and some Lasombra, Nosferatu and Toreador have taken an interest in the work.
